statement: You are given two strings, first and second. A subsequence is what remains after deleting zero or more characters without changing the order of the rest.
Find a longest string that is a subsequence of both first and second, and return the string itself rather than its length.
When several different longest common subsequences exist, any one of them is a correct answer.

examples.explanation: b, d and e appear in this order in both strings. The longest common subsequence has length 3, and "bde" is the only one.
The length is 2, and "ab" is the only common subsequence of that length: "ca" and "cb" do not appear in order in "abac".
Both "ab" and "ac" are common subsequences of length 2, and no common subsequence is longer. Either one is a correct answer; this trace returns "ab".
